finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[AUTH-1] Missing index on clerkId → full table scans
File: prisma/schema.prisma (L9-L28)
Evidence: The User model stores clerkId as a plain String without @unique or @@index; multiple API handlers (e.g. admin/check-admin, abandoned-carts) perform prisma.user.findFirst({ where: { clerkId: userId } }) which will require a table scan as users grow.  
Impact: Every admin/auth-mapping request causes a full users table scan at scale, guaranteed to saturate DB CPU / IOPS as user rows increase.  
Fix: Add an index or unique constraint on clerkId (e.g. clerkId String? @unique or @@index([clerkId])) and run a migration; backfill existing values.

[AUTH-2] Middleware can bypass auth when Clerk is misconfigured or errors
File: src/middleware.ts (L11-L40)
Evidence: The middleware returns NextResponse.next() when NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY is missing and also catches all errors and continues the request, effectively skipping protection for protected routes.  
Impact: A missing env var or transient middleware error can expose /api/admin/* and /admin routes site-wide (trust-boundary failure), leading to complete admin/account compromise.  
Fix: Fail closed: return a 5xx or redirect to an error/sign-in page on missing config or middleware errors, and alert on missing critical env at startup.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[AUTH-3] Repeated per-request DB lookup for clerkId without cache
File: src/app/api/admin/check-admin/route.ts (L1-L40)
Evidence: Handlers call auth() then immediately run prisma.user.findFirst({ where: { clerkId: userId } }) on every request instead of caching or using Clerk server SDK to fetch required user metadata.  
Impact: Even with an index, this creates hot DB traffic on every protected endpoint and multiplies load with concurrent admin or dashboard usage.  
Fix: Cache clerkId→user mapping (in process cache or Redis) or use Clerk server APIs that return required attributes in the auth token, avoiding DB lookups on every request.

[AUTH-4] Webhook does synchronous DB upserts and lacks persisted idempotency
File: src/app/api/webhooks/clerk/route.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: The Svix-verified webhook handler directly runs prisma.user.create / update / upsert for each event and does not persist processed event IDs to protect against retries/replays.  
Impact: A burst of webhook deliveries or retries can spike DB writes (upserts), causing write amplification and contention; replayed deliveries may cause repeated processing.  
Fix: Persist Svix event ID (or use a processed_events table) to deduplicate, and push user-sync jobs to a background queue to make webhook handling non-blocking.

--- INFO ---

[AUTH-5] Guest-order users created with empty clerkId
File: src/app/api/checkout/create-order/route.ts
Evidence: create-order creates guest users with clerkId: '' for orders without Clerk auth.
